transcript.text: Thanks everyone for being here. As we kick off this review, I want to make sure we cover the standard bases before I give final approval. We all know the replacement ephemeral runner system passed build-speed and failure-recovery tests in staging, and that the draft policy currently allows 20 concurrent jobs with 30-day log retention. But I'm noticing the draft doesn't mention immutable log storage or build-provenance attestations. Before we go further, I'd like to hear from each of you on your respective areas of concern so we can decide whether the policy needs revisions before publication.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: There's a critical issue we need to address before this policy goes forward. Yesterday, while helping the release team debug a separate build, I confirmed that the production release pipeline uses privileged Docker-in-Docker, which cannot run on the proposed ephemeral runner profile. The workable design is exactly two isolated persistent runners dedicated to release jobs, with the remaining jobs on ephemeral runners. I haven't updated the platform proposal yet, but this directly affects the concurrency and runner architecture assumptions in the draft policy.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: During an unrelated queue investigation this morning, I measured a campaign-day burst of 28 simultaneous CI jobs. The safe production ceiling is exactly 32 concurrent jobs, and the queue should generate an alert when it exceeds 24 jobs. For the policy, 32 is the max_concurrent_jobs value to use; 28 is only the observed burst that motivates raising the draft limit. I haven't added those measurements to the capacity dashboard yet.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: While preparing evidence for an audit this afternoon, I confirmed that build logs for the organization's regulated release repositories must be retained for exactly 180 days in immutable storage and that each production build must produce a signed provenance attestation. I have not opened the compliance ticket yet. This directly conflicts with the draft policy's 30-day log retention and lack of provenance attestation requirements.

commitments.detail: Update the draft operating policy to reflect the hybrid runner architecture with two isolated persistent runners for release jobs and ephemeral runners for all other jobs, max_concurrent_jobs of 32, queue alert threshold of 24, 180-day immutable log retention, and signed provenance attestations for production builds before publication.
Update the platform proposal to incorporate the two isolated persistent runners dedicated to release jobs alongside the ephemeral runner pool.
Add the capacity measurements (28-job observed burst, 32-job safe ceiling, 24-job alert threshold) to the capacity dashboard.
Open the compliance ticket documenting the 180-day immutable log retention and signed provenance attestation requirements for regulated release repositories.
